topic: Nonmodifying Algorithms in C++ Standard Library
explanation: Nonmodifying algorithms are a category of algorithms in the C++ Standard Library that operate on input ranges without altering the elements or their order. They are used for read-only operations such as searching, comparing, or counting elements. These algorithms work with input and forward iterators, making them applicable to all standard containers. They are essential for performing safe, side-effect-free data processing, especially when the integrity of the data must be preserved.
keywords: STL nonmodifying, C++ read-only algorithms, Side-effect-free algorithms
